Photo from Getty Images 497850401 24 | Advanced Computing Annual Report 2025 Advanced Computing Annual Report 2025 | 25 Faster Discovery of Efficient Thermoelectric Materials with ML Thermoelectric materials convert heat into electricity and vice versa, enabling cooling and waste heat recovery—two key pathways to improving energy efficiency across industrial, transportation, and consumer technologies. Supported by the National Science Foundation, researchers use HPC and ML to accelerate the discovery and optimization of Zintl phase thermoelectric materials with improved stability and efficiency. Zintl phases are intermetallic compounds that rank among the best performing thermoelectric materials. Leveraging HPC, researchers previously identified more than 1,800 new Zintl phases, laying the groundwork for rapid materials screening. This work was published in the Journal of Materials Chemistry A.7 Building on this foundation, the team developed a motif-based design strategy that treats atomic substructure like Lego-style building blocks for assembling new compounds. GPU- accelerated ML workflows on Kestrel then automated the combination and evaluation of these motifs, rapidly identifying promising new thermoelectric materials. This approach complements detailed thermodynamic modeling demonstrated in recent work published in Advanced Functional Materials,8 where first-principles simulations helped explain large variations in electron concentrations and guided synthesis conditions that enhance performance.
